title: Naturality of the supported Hom identification under base change
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $h:T'\to T$ a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and
$i:D\hookrightarrow T$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Choose schemes $D',V',V$
and maps $i':D'\hookrightarrow T'$, $h_D:D'\to D$, $v:V\hookrightarrow T$, $v':V'\hookrightarrow T'$
and $h_V:V'\to V$ such that $(h_D,i',i,h)$ and $(h_V,v',v,h)$ are pullback squares
[def-pc-fibre-product], and $V,V'$ are the open complements of $D,D'$.
Work in ordinary small etale module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], using
inverse and direct image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and constant
sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. There are canonical restriction chain maps $q,q'$,
a canonical closed-immersion exchange $e:h^{-1}i_*A_D\to i'_*A_{D'}$, and natural cone
comparisons identifying the shifted restriction cones with derived Hom from the closed constant
sheaves [lem-amb-closed-support-hom]. The exchange is an isomorphism. For every bounded-below
complex $K$ of $A_T$-module sheaves and integer $q$, the induced relative-section pullback
$P_h$ satisfies
$$\Phi_{T',D',h^{-1}K}^q(P_h x)=
(h^{-1}\Phi_{T,D,K}^q(x))\circ e^{-1},$$
where $\Phi$ is the canonical supported-Hom identification. The same identifications make
forgetting support equal to precomposition by the constant unit $A_T\to i_*A_D$.
Here the constant coefficient, unit and exchange are the unrestricted helper constructions of [def-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-kummer-class] and [def-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer-boundary]. On functorial degreewise-injective K-injective models I and J, the resolution comparison a:h^{-1}I→J extends the pulled-back resolution unit. The two section maps are section pullback followed by a; their diagonal shifted-cone map defines P_h. The supported Hom map sends c to a∘h^{-1}c∘e^{-1}. The cone comparison is normalized by the kernel inclusion c↦(0,c∘η), using evaluation at 1 to identify Hom(A_T,I) with global sections. Forgetting support is projection of this shifted cone to Γ(T,I), with that fixed target.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], $i'$ is a closed immersion. Write $h_D:D'\to D$. Form the exchange $h^{-1}i_*F\to i'_*h_D^{-1}F$ for an abelian sheaf $F$ using [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange]. At a geometric point $\bar t'$ in $D'$, [lemma-openclosed-stalk-upperstar] and [lemma-openclosed-stalk-lowerstar] identify both stalks with $F_{h_D\bar t'}$; the section-restriction formula for exchange sends each germ to itself. Off $D'$, both stalks are zero: the source is computed over $T-D$ and the target over $T'-D'$, where the closed fibre product is empty, so their direct images evaluate to zero by [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Thus [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] makes the exchange an isomorphism. Apply this to the underlying abelian sheaf of $A_D$. The exchange is $A$-linear because restriction commutes with the scalar actions. The canonical constant coefficient identification $h_D^{-1}A_D=A_{D'}$ from [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] gives precisely the asserted $e$.

Let $\eta:A_T\to i_*A_D$ and $\eta':A_{T'}\to i'_*A_{D'}$ be the constant adjunction units. Under $h^{-1}A_T=A_{T'}$, one has $e\circ h^{-1}\eta=\eta'$. Indeed the exchange formula of [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] first pulls a constant section to the closed fibre product and then restricts it, so the two composites send each local constant $a$ to its constant restriction $a$. These maps on the sheafified constant presheaf determine the sheaf maps by [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. The coefficient identifications and adjunctions here are those of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact].

The categories $\Mod(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $\Mod(T'_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ are Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-grothendieck-abelian]. Choose $K\xrightarrow{u}I$ by [lem-pur-kinjective-degreewise-existence], with $I$ K-injective and termwise injective. Exactness of $h^{-1}$ in [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] makes $h^{-1}u$ a quasi-isomorphism. Apply the same resolution theorem on $T'$ to $h^{-1}I$ to obtain a quasi-isomorphism $a:h^{-1}I\to J$, with $J$ K-injective and termwise injective. Thus $a\circ h^{-1}u$ resolves $h^{-1}K$. All comparisons below use this actual chain map $a$.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact] to $A_T$ and use the constant coefficient identifications of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. It gives $0\to v_!A_V\to A_T\xrightarrow{\eta}i_*A_D\to0$. Put $C_I^n=\Hom_T(i_*A_D,I^n)$, $E_I^n=\Hom_T(A_T,I^n)$, and $B_I^n=\Hom_T(v_!A_V,I^n)$, with differential postcomposition by $d_I$. Then $0\to C_I\xrightarrow{k_I}E_I\xrightarrow{r_I}B_I\to0$ is a degreewise short exact sequence of complexes: factoring through the cokernel gives the kernel assertion, and the extension property in [def-sp-injective-resolutions] gives surjectivity of $r_I^n$. The adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] identifies $B_I^n=\Gamma(V,v^{-1}I^n)$ and $E_I^n=\Gamma(T,I^n)$; a map from the constant rank-one module is determined by its value on $1$, and a section $s$ defines $a\mapsto as$. The adjunction's counit formula identifies $r_I$ with restriction, and $k_I$ is precomposition by $\eta$. Repeat these definitions and assertions on $T'$ with $J$, obtaining $C_J,E_J,B_J,k_J,r_J$.

By [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] and [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact], $v^{-1}$ is right adjoint to an exact functor, so [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] makes $v^{-1}I$ K-injective. The same applies to $v'^{-1}J$. Both are resolutions of the restricted coefficient complexes, since inverse image is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] to termwise sections and to termwise $\Hom(i_*A_D,-)$; these functors commute with shifts and cones by their additive formulas. Consequently $E_I,B_I,C_I$ compute $R\Gamma(T,K),R\Gamma(V,K|_V),R\Hom_T(i_*A_D,K)$ respectively, and the primed complexes compute their counterparts. The required existence of K-injectives on the open schemes follows by the same two nodes used in step 3, applied to $V,V'$.

Use the cone convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $F_I=\Cone(r_I)[-1]$, so $F_I^n=B_I^{n-1}\oplus E_I^n$ and $d(b,s)=(-d_Bb-r_I(s),d_Es)$. The map $\iota_I:C_I\to F_I$, $c\mapsto(0,k_Ic)$, is a quasi-isomorphism. To check surjectivity on cohomology, given a cocycle $(b,s)$, choose $t\in E_I^{n-1}$ with $r_I(t)=-b$. Subtracting $d(0,t)$ gives $(0,s-d_Et)$ with $s-d_Et\in\ker r_I$. For injectivity, if $(0,k_Ic)=d(b,s)$, choose $t\in E_I^{n-2}$ with $r_I(t)=b$; then $s+d_Et\in\ker r_I$ has differential $k_Ic$. Thus $c$ is a boundary in $C_I$. The same applies to $J$. This realizes the canonical identification of [lem-amb-closed-support-hom]: apply Hom to the constant open-closed sequence with its specified unit and counit, and use the inclusion of its kernel into the shifted restriction cone. On $H^q$ its inverse, followed by the derived-Hom interpretation, is $\Phi^q$.

proof.text: For a degree-$n$ morphism $c:i_*A_D\to I^n$, define $f_C(c)=a^n\circ h^{-1}c\circ e^{-1}$. Define $f_E(s)=a^n\circ h^{-1}s$ under the constant coefficient identification. Define $f_B$ by pullback of sections on $V$, followed by restriction of $a$ to $V'$; identify $v'^{-1}h^{-1}=h_V^{-1}v^{-1}$, where $h_V:V'\to V$ is the restricted morphism. These are chain maps since $a$ commutes with differentials. Restricting a pulled-back section is its pulled-back restriction, so $r_J f_E=f_B r_I$ by the sectionwise definition of inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Step 2 gives $f_E k_I=k_J f_C$: for $c$, both sides equal $a h^{-1}c\,h^{-1}\eta$, since $e^{-1}\eta'=h^{-1}\eta$. Thus the map of shifted cones is the actual diagonal chain map $f_F(b,s)=(f_Bb,f_Es)$, and $f_F\iota_I=\iota_J f_C$ holds strictly.

source.place: Penultimate paragraph: “All the cone maps and Kummer boundaries commute with pullback of the pair”; chain-level verification of the cone-map assertion

proof.text: The map $f_F$ computes the specified relative pullback $P_h$: its two components are the section pullbacks followed by the resolution comparison $a$, and their square with restriction commutes strictly. This choice has the usual resolution-independent meaning. Indeed [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] identifies maps into the K-injective target $J$ with derived maps. Hence any other comparison into $J$ representing the same derived coefficient map is homotopic to $a$. A homotopy induces maps $s_E,s_B$ of degree $-1$ with $r_Js_E=s_Br_I$, and on shifted cones $S(b,s)=(-s_Bb,s_Es)$ satisfies $dS+Sd=f_F-\widetilde f_F$, by the displayed cone differential. Additivity of pullback gives the same assertion for the supported Hom complexes. Replacing $I$ or $J$ by another resolution gives homotopy-equivalent K-injective targets by the same cited lemma; these comparisons identify the maps just constructed. Thus no arbitrary lift of a square in the triangulated category is being chosen.

source.place: Tag 070I, lemma-K-injective, morphisms in the localized category; explicit compatible cone homotopy

proof.text: For every integer $q$, a cocycle $c\in C_I^q$ is a chain map $i_*A_D[0]\to I[q]$, and a boundary is exactly a null-homotopic such map. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], localization identifies $H^q(C_I)$ with $\Hom_{D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)}(i_*A_D,K[q])$; the same holds on $T'$. The shift convention is that of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; a cocycle into $I^q$ gives the degree-zero component of the map into $I[q]$. In the derived category $a$ identifies $h^{-1}I$ with the chosen representative $J$ of $h^{-1}K$. Therefore $H^q(f_C)$ sends the class $\alpha$ to $(h^{-1}\alpha)\circ e^{-1}$. Apply $H^q$ to the strict identity $f_F\iota_I=\iota_J f_C$ of step 7 and invert $H^q(\iota_I),H^q(\iota_J)$ from step 6. This gives $\Phi^q_{T',D',h^{-1}K}(P_hx)=(h^{-1}\Phi^q_{T,D,K}(x))\circ e^{-1}$, as required.

source.place: Penultimate paragraph: supported Hom identification and base-change compatibility

proof.text: Forgetting support on the relative section complex is the projection $p_I:F_I\to E_I$, $(b,s)\mapsto s$, using [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Since $p_I\iota_I=k_I$ and $k_I(c)=c\circ\eta$ by step 4, the identification of step 6 makes forgetting support exactly precomposition by $A_T\xrightarrow{\eta}i_*A_D$, in every degree. This also holds on $T'$. The unit identity in step 2 and the map of complexes in step 7 show that these forgetting maps commute with pullback.

Step checks: (1) the stalk identity on D' comes from the upperstar and lowerstar nodes; off D' both stalks are 0 by the direct-image formula, because h^{-1}D=D' as sets; conservativity finishes it. (2) The unit compatibility e∘h^{-1}η=η' holds on constant sections. (3) Resolutions are redone on T', so pullback is not assumed to preserve injectives. (4) The Hom sequence 0→C→E→B→0 is exact on the right by injectivity, and the counit formula makes the map restriction. (5) The 08BJ hypotheses are met: v_! is exact and left adjoint to v^{-1}. (6) I recomputed the sign of Cone(r)[-1] from def-weil-abstract-derived-category: d(b,s)=(-d_B b - r s, d_E s). Both lifts for the kernel-inclusion quasi-isomorphism are correct, and the normalization matches the parent's construction (c↦(0,c)) and the blueprint. (7) Both squares of chain maps commute strictly. (8) The cone homotopy (-s_B,s_E) is correct. (9) The derived reading of H^q(f_C) and the inverted ι give the formula. statement_change.old_statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $h:T'\to T$ a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $i:D\hookrightarrow T$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and $i':D'=T'\times_TD\hookrightarrow T'$ its scheme-theoretic pullback [def-pc-fibre-product]. Put $V=T-D$ and $V'=T'-D'$. Work in ordinary small etale module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], using inverse and direct image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. The canonical closed-immersion exchange $e:h^{-1}i_*A_D\to i'_*A_{D'}$ is an isomorphism. For every bounded-below complex $K$ of $A_T$-module sheaves and integer $q$, in the abstract derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] put
$$H^q(T,V;K)=H^q(\operatorname{Cone}(R\Gamma(T,K)\to R\Gamma(V,K|_V))[-1]),$$
with etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. Use the canonical supported-Hom identification [lem-amb-closed-support-hom] $\Phi_{T,D,K}^q:H^q(T,V;K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)}(i_*A_D,K[q])$. Then pullback $P_h$ on the relative section complexes satisfies
$$\Phi_{T',D',h^{-1}K}^q(P_h x)=(h^{-1}\Phi_{T,D,K}^q(x))\circ e^{-1}.$$
Here $P_h$ is induced by the canonical derived section pullback maps on $T$ and $V$, with their restriction-compatible comparison. The same identifications make forgetting support equal to precomposition by the constant unit $A_T\to i_*A_D$.
statement_change.what: The old statement left the complements and comparison maps implicit. The explicit formulation introduces their scheme maps and pullback squares and specifies the actual operations on K-injective representatives. The returned existential interface did not fix these operations: zero or rescaled maps could satisfy its equations. The repair fixes the exchange to the published mate, the resolution comparison to an extension of the resolution unit, the relative pullback to the diagonal cone map, the Hom pullback to inverse-image/precomposition, the cone isomorphism to the kernel-inclusion normalization, and forgetting support to projection to global sections. The additional dependencies supply already-published unrestricted constant/unit/exchange helpers; no finite coefficient or Cartier-divisor hypothesis is added.
